1: [ translation by franz meladOro / fra@melad.org ] Rabbi Hezekiah began with the beauty of the opening, and in the radiance of the rose/lily, the truth is that its buds correspond to the thirteen letters following the Name of God, and the ‘H’s’ above the Name of God correspond to the letters following the Name of God, as he concludes: ‘What is the rose, etc.’ The Ari, of blessed memory, wrote that ‘rose’ has the gematria of ‘Esther’, and the secret of Esther is the point of Malchut in Atzilut, in the secret of ‘Go and make yourself small’; and she is concealed at the head of creation, and therefore she is called Esther; and as R. Meir states in the portion of ‘Ki Teitzei’ that the Holy One, blessed be He, concealed her from Ahasuerus, and it is said: ‘And My glory I will not give to another.’ And the explanation of the verse is as follows: just as the physical rose stands amongst the thorns, which are nothing in comparison to it, so too is my beloved, who is the ‘M’ of Atzilut, amongst the daughters—that is, her seven maidens, who are the seven palaces of creation:

Indeed, the Knesset Yisrael embodies both judgement and mercy, as explained by the Ari, of blessed memory, that whilst the primary structure of the Nukva is derived from the Gevurot, she is nonetheless also built from the Chesed, for her two lines are formed from the revealed Chesed of the Danah of Zeir Anpin: The mercy of Netzach is half for itself and half for the right line of the Nukva; likewise, the mercy of Hod is half for itself and half for the left line of the Nukva. And from the two-thirds of revealed mercy found in the two-thirds of Tiferet, the Nukva takes one-third for her Keter; and this is what is meant by the statement that ‘there is judgement and mercy within her’:

In it are the thirteen vessels of mercy, as explained by the Ari z”l in the Kavanot of Hanukkah (and alluded to in the book Mishnat Chassidim, folio 127b, Chapter 2) Behold, there are thirteen words in this blessing corresponding to the thirteen vessels of mercy, for the Mother adorns the daughter in the secret of the Hanukkah candle, as ‘Chana’ is the Mother, whose numerical value is 63, and ‘K’u’ is the Shekhinah; and through this, the splendour of Zeir Anpin is rectified in the eight primordial vessels, from ‘El’ to ‘Nitzar Chesed’ on the eighth days, and the eighth day awakens all the attributes through the union of ‘Nitzor’ and ‘Nekah’; therefore, on each day of Hanukkah, one should focus on the first day in relation to the second—‘Rachum’ etc.—and on the eighth day, one should focus on ‘Nitzor Chesed’ up to ‘Nekah’. End of quote. It is clear, then, that there is a connection between the thirteen vessels of mercy and the daughter, who is the Kingdom. He further wrote that in the Priestly Blessing there are thirteen ‘yuds’ corresponding to the thirteen Tikunim of the beard of Abba, and within them there are nine ‘vav’s’ corresponding to the nine Tikunim of the beard of Z’A, and six ‘he’s’ corresponding to the six Tikunim of the Nukva, and all of this extends to the Shekhinah, as it is written: ‘And Your pious ones shall bless thus,’ and the pious ones are the priests, and this is ‘Thus shall you bless’:

It is known from every source that the purpose of the Dikna d’A”A is to enforce the laws in order to sweeten the laws of the Kingdom, so that the external forces may not draw sustenance from it; and this is what is meant by ‘they guard it’—in order to protect them from the external forces:

Oh God, here, from the moment it is mentioned, there are thirteen letters; these are the thirteen vessels of mercy that the Mother—who is called Aelohim—brought forth, for the Mother received them from the Ancient One, and from her they went to the Mem; therefore, the name of Aelohim is not mentioned again in the Torah until these thirteen letters were written:

The five strong leaves surrounding the rose are the green leaves that encircle the physical rose, and they allude to the five letters of ‘Mantsafach’, which receive the letter ‘Mem’ from the Mother. And this is what the late Rabbi stated regarding the blessing ‘HaRav et Ribono’ (as alluded to in Sefer 48, page 131b, paragraph 11): Five times ‘N’un’ corresponds to the five letters of ‘M-N-T-Z-P-K’, all of which have become our aid; therefore, the vowelisation of the blessing with the ‘Shva’ is the vowelisation of Gevurah, and the end of the blessing, ‘Y-H-V-H’, is vowelised as ‘Elohim’. Rachel, the cup in the hand of the Lord, is the rose seated upon the five strong leaves given to her by Binah to save her: And this is what is stated in the Zohar: ‘And these five are called “salvations”, and these five are called “restraints”; for the Rav wrote that the fifty gates of understanding are the five acts of kindness, each comprising ten, totalling fifty; and likewise the five acts of might, each comprising ten, totalling fifty.’ And here Rabbi Hezekiah, of blessed memory, explains the five acts of might. And this is the wording of the Ari z”l: ‘The cup of the blessing after meals should be placed upon the five fingers of the right hand; these are the secret of the five sweetened Strengths, and they are the five petals of the rose.’ End of quote. And in the book ‘Arugat HaBosem’, on page 85b, it is written that the Five Powers of the lower Mem are the five strong leaves that surround the upper Mem, which is the secret of the Bride of Moses. And the Five Powers guard the Mem from the external forces, and they are called ‘Yeshuot’ (Salvations), which save the maiden; and in the Book of Genesis, this is the true secret.:
Literally "The light was created":

"And it was concealed" — meaning that the five Chassadim (lovingkindnesses) do not emerge uncovered from the mouth of the Yesod of Imma (Mother); rather, a thin garment is made for them, and wherever they travel, they take their garment with them — as the Rav wrote in the book Otzrot Chayyim [The Arizal hardly ever wrote at all (however, the Cairo Geniza has recently surfaced several piyutim that he wrote while living in Egypt). Thus, his teachings come to us from the students who learned from him during his short time in Tzfat. Most of these teachings were written by his closest disciple, R. Chaim Vital. There are, however, books by other students such as Sefer HaKavanot (R. Trinko), Kanfei Yonah ( R. Menachem Azariah of Fano), and Emek HaMelech (R. Seruk). The most important, and perhaps most complex, of R. Vital's works are the Etz Chaim books (Etz Chaim, Pri Etz Chaim, and Nof Etz Chaim books). Much of the work deals with kavanot and secrets for mitzvot, as well as laying down the foundations of Lurianic kabbalah. The Shmoneh Shearim are the "eight gates" that are considered less complicated, often go over the Etz Chaim topics, but also range into Tanakh, Gemarah, meditation, Zohar, and reincarnation (they are Shaar Hagilgulim, Hakavanot, Hahakdamot, Hamitzvot, Hapsukim, Maamarei Rashbi, Maamarei Rashbi, and Shaar Ruach Hakodesh). They are each separate works, but generally stick to R. Vital's teachings. Otzarot Chaim is from another category: those edited by R. Yaakov Tzemach (he was R. Meir Pepperos's student, who edited the Etz Chaim books). It incorporates other students of the Arizal besides R. Vital in framing the system of kabbalah. The best first texts to approach the Arizal, are the Etz Chaim, Shaar Hahakdamot, and Mavo Shearim (also ed. by R. Tzemach). Etz Chaim is really the foundation of foundations on the Arizal, and according to R. Aryeh Kaplan, "for one who has mastered the contents of this work, the rest is essentially revealed." Shaar Hahakdamot repeats many of themes of Etz Chaim, as does Mavo Shearim (which does mean Introduction to the Gates). Thus, those 3 works are usually the first works studied. One last note; the very name of kabbalah indicates that such learning need be taught by those capable and fluent in them. A reliable, smicha rabbi is called to the task for one proven to have already filled his stomach with the bread and meat of Jewish sustenance: Tanakh, Mishnah, Gemarah, Halachah, Rishonim and Achronim. B'Hatzlacha. Answer from Aryeh on Stack Exchange. ]

"And it was included in the covenant" — this refers to Yesod of Ze'ir Anpin, in which the Chassadim are all contained. Further, it is my humble opinion (nir'eh li) that the light that was created corresponds to the root of the Chassadim within Da'at; and "it was hidden" corresponds to their extension through the body of Ze'ir Anpin; and each individual Chesed was concealed within one of the minor limbs (mochin u'ketanim); and "it was included in the covenant" corresponds to their collective unity within Yesod.

"And this is called etz oseh pri (a tree that makes fruit). It is known that etz oseh pri is Yesod, and etz pri (a fruit tree) is [the sefirah of] Mem [i.e., Malkhut] — as stated in the Zohar, Parashat Vayechi, folio 238a, and in Sefer [Etz Chayyim], folio 130, side 8 (?), chapter 2, paragraph 3, where it is written as follows: 'From the Yesod of Tevunah — which surrounds the Yesod of Abba at the beginning of the place of its emergence from the body — there emerged Ester, whose numerical value is [that of] Shoshanah (שושנה), and it equals [the value of] Adonai spelled out (מלא) minus the letter Yod — which is the secret of the essential self-point (nekudat atzmo ha-atzmit) that conceals itself at the head of [the world of] Beriah, and it is the Yod of Adonai.' — End of his language. And in [Etz] Chayyim, folio 106b. And see in the Zohar, Parashat Balak, folio 185b, and what the Ramaz wrote on it in [the passage beginning] Adonai mi ya'amod; and in the Zohar, Parashat Va'era, folio 23a, and what the Ramaz wrote on it; and in Parashat Pinchas, folio 233b; and in Ha'azinu, folio 286b — and then you will truly understand the inner intention of this passage."

The portrait of the Divine was formed in 42 pairs, and the Rabbi said: ‘Behold, after there was the supreme pairing of Arich in Wisdom—which is the hidden mind—with Binah, which is the throat, the drop descended from there, from the 82 of Arich’s Wisdom, and passed through the 63, a mere passage, and descended to the 45 and the ‘N’ of the wisdom of Arich, and there it received a root from both of them, which is the root of Zon: And it is known that every drop is YHVH, which comes from Chabad, and the YHVH of 72 is clothed within the YHVH of 45, and the YHVH of 45 is clothed within the YHVH of 50, which is Yod, Heh, Vav, totalling 42; and there is no drop descending from above without two drops ascending to meet it: Now, in the throat of Arich, which is Binah, there are six ‘Ahiyah’. Two ‘Ahiyah’ of Yud-Yud in the first three, and two of Aleph in Chagat. And the two ‘Ahiyah’ of the ‘Heh’ are in the ‘Neh’i’: and the ‘Man’ ascend from below to above, and the two ‘Ahiyah’ of the ‘Heh’ are clothed in the two ‘Ahiyah’ of the ‘Alphin’, and the ‘Alphin’ in the ‘Yud-Yudim’: and the ‘Ahiyah’ of the ‘Yud-Yudim’ is simple and full, the filling of the filling being 42 letters including the ‘Kollel’: And the male drop is included within the female; thus, the two ‘Ahiyah’ are twice forty-two, and this is what is stated in the portion of Genesis: ‘And as many as the image of the covenant, forty-two pairs were sown in it’—meaning that the foundation of Arich, called the Covenant, was sown with forty-two pairs, that is to say, twice forty-two: Even if we wish to interpret ‘Yah-Hu’ as having a gematria of 42, and the two simple ‘Ah-Yah’, this still amounts to 42 pairs. Thus concluded the late Rabbi, and this is alluded to in Masechet Makkot 13a, Chapter 2. And this matter is akin to the forty-two pairings effected in the union of Abba and Imma, as stated there in Machon HaChokmah, chapter 12, page 2b, section 3, paragraph 6 And the text reads: ‘And all the pairings of Abba and Imma are effected by the unifying intellect, their forty-two pairings, which connects the forty-two of the ‘Sefirot’ of Abba with the forty-two of ‘Ahiyah’—which is the ‘Ahiyah’ of Imma—and thus forty-two pairs are formed.’ And on folio 13 of the aforementioned tractate, it is written that the forty-two pairings of Arich are the YHVH of Ben, which totals forty-two. And in 2:161, ‘Ehyeh of Yud-Yud-Yud’: the sum of their two roots is 42, as stated there. And it seems to me that this is why he wrote ‘the image of the Covenant’, for ‘Arich’ does not actually bear the name of the Covenant itself, but rather ‘the image of the Covenant’, as it is merely the tip of the Yud; and how can letters and names be assigned to it, as in the case of the ‘Zayir’?

Thus, ‘I fear lest a letter be revealed, etc.’—as the Rav wrote in *Kohelet Ya’akov*, twenty-two letters from them form the ‘Z’ir’ body, and the ten ‘Havayot’ of the ‘Tagin’, which correspond to the Ten Commandments, are the ‘Z’ir’ soul; and the ten ‘Havayot’ made of dots are the ‘Z’ir’ spirit. The totality of them all is forty-two, and the soul is from the Mother, and the spirit from the Father. And from these forty-two letters were created all the worlds—body, soul and spirit. And this is what is meant by ‘Thus I tremble, lest…’. And in that exegesis of the forty-two pairs, the Rabbi explained that the name ‘forty-two’ derives from the ‘bet’ of ‘Bereshit’ to the ‘bet’ of ‘v’bohu’ (as mentioned above). And it seems to me that he likened the Kingdom specifically to a rose amongst thorns, which resembles it in all these analogies, and not to other roses; and in the parable, too, there are Kingdoms of the worlds of BY”A, but the verse speaks of the of Atzilut; therefore, he said, ‘My beloved, she is the 40 of Atzilut; amongst the daughters are those of BY”A, who are all called ‘daughters’ because they are feminine, as is known from the words of the Rav, of blessed memory, and they do not possess such purity as the 40 of Atzilut, nor do they possess the 13 long-lasting vessels nor the five mights of the Mother. And this is similar to what the Ramaz wrote in Ha’azinu, p. 66b; see there. She is also called ‘the rose of the valleys’ to allude to the hint mentioned in the parashah of Emor on folio 107a; see there:

And the Ramaz explains this statement here as well in terms of the three aspects of the lights revealed in the Arich: the mouth, the navel and the covenant; and in his central line is the conduit that permeates the entire world of Atzilut:

He prefaced this with three preliminaries: first, that the mouth is the ‘mem’, as stated in Sha’ar Arich, Chapter 8; second, that within the hidden wisdom there is an inner union of the palate and the throat, and the light of this union bursts forth and is revealed from the mouth outwards; and likewise, the secret of the thirteen Tikunei Dikna is from the ‘Machas’. Thirdly, the Sefirot are rectified from the might of the Ancient of Days and clothed by Him; therefore, the Name ‘Elohim’ is required in every instance. Likewise, the thirteen attributes correspond to the secret of the thirteen letters of the full Name ‘Elohim’. The simple Name ‘Elohim’ is also found in the beard. In the first rectification, ‘YH’; in the sixth rectification, ‘M’; in the twelfth rectification, ‘H’; and ‘S’. And the verse alludes to the secret of the three ‘Rishin’ in Genesis, the secret of the ‘Keter d’Arich’, which is the first in the World of Atzilut, for above it lies the World of Ein Sof. ‘He created’ is the secret of the first ‘Rishin’; ‘the second’ is the secret of ‘Air’, and since it is concealed—being a radiance from the knowledge of the Ancient of Days—it is therefore stated simply: ‘He created’; who created? ‘Elohim’ is the secret of the ‘Chok’ which begins to be revealed through the mouth, as stated. And it alludes to the fact that this is a holy mouth surrounded by the thirteen vessels of mercy, whose root lies in the ancient kings, who are from the name ‘Ben’. The name ‘Elohim’ also has the secret of ‘Ben’, in the secret known to us concerning the ‘Sons of God’, for the five letters of ‘Elohim’ are simple:

And the full form is thirteen, and the filling of the filling is thirty-four; all of this is ‘Ben’, meaning ‘between the daughters’. And for this aspect, the name ‘My Beloved’ is fitting, for the union of the mouth is the very essence of unity and constancy. And from there, all the Sefirot are shepherded. And it is said, ‘By your word shall all the nations drink’. Behold, before you are the thirteen corrections encompassing the first aspect for the revelation of the Light, which is the mouth, which is the Kingdom:

The second aspect: the five upper, encircling branches that surround the rose, as explained by the Ari, of blessed memory (and alluded to in the ‘Maharal’ on Tractate Tazria, page 89b, Chapter 4, Paragraph 1) (and also alluded to in the ‘Maharal’ on page 9, Chapter 1, Paragraph 2), that the foundation of the Ancient One It ends at the chest of Arich, and the Rach”u, of blessed memory, wrote that this foundation is the Nukva d’Atik. And behold, first the five Gevurot emerge from the mouth of this foundation, and afterwards the Chesed come and push them outwards; and the Gevurot encircle the Chesed, and this is the meaning of ‘reproach is better than open rebuke’, and this is what is intended in our discourse; for after the conclusion of the mention of the thirteen Tikunim of the Dikna, which ends at the chest of Arich, then ‘Elohim’ is mentioned a second time in five words—these are the five Gevurot we have mentioned—and from here they are given to the Mother; and they are the secret of the ‘N’ gates. But here, these five gates are the secret of the five Gevurot that surround the Chesed, and it is known that at the height of Ze’ir’s greatness, he becomes the crown of Matat Arich. And this is the place where the foundation of Nukva d’Atik concludes. And since Rachel is equal to the Ze’ir, her crown is also there. It is known that the main structure of her body is from the Mahag, and therefore the vessel of her crown is made from these five wondrous Gevurot. And then she is like a rose surrounded by five firm leaves, for the crown is a circumference, as it is written, ‘They encircled Benjamin’. And this cup, which receives from the male Sefirot, is called ‘the cup of blessing’. For the male Sefirot is ‘Blessed’ and the female Sefirot is ‘Blessing’, and the numerical value of ‘cup’ is ‘Elohim’; but here it is the ‘cup of blessing’ because it receives the elevation of these Gevurot, and furthermore, they are special and encompass the Chesed, and therefore it is placed on the right. And of this it is said, ‘I will lift up the cup of salvation’—which is simply the cup. In the realm of kingship, the act of lifting the cup is to draw from this lofty and exalted source:

Examination C The revelation of the Light is that which is revealed in its essence, without any diminution or alteration; it is the seed-drop that emanates from the mouth of the Mother. The hidden Light for the righteous is that which extends along the entire central line of the Ancient of Days and the Long One. The males of the Ancient of Days are clothed in the Long One, and the Long One in the Father, and the Father in the Father, and the Father in the Small One; and the Small One influences Rachel. Therefore, ‘Let there be light’ (Gimel). 72, 63, 45, 2, 1 is the secret of the male drop. ‘And let there be light’ (Gimel) refers to Rachel, who receives them at her foundation. Corresponding to this, within the rose there is her seed, hidden within it; and it is said of this holy seed, ‘Da’itbari’—that is, its existence is derived from the Moachin—and it is hidden, not revealed at the navel in the chest, but rather spreads along the spinal cord and branches out in the Chagatna in the secret of the five letters of ‘Chesed’. And afterwards, everything is encompassed within the Covenant, which is called ‘All’. And since this light does not change, it is therefore said, ‘And that seed endures in the very letter of the Covenant’, to rule out the notion that it is merely an illumination. The general scope of this discourse begins with the aspect of the first Kingdom, which is revealed in Atzilut—the secret of the mouth—and concludes with Rachel, who is the last. And to complete this exposition, it is said:

And as for the ‘Portrait of the Covenant’, this will be explained in the commentary on the ‘42 Pairings’ written by the Ari, of blessed memory, which refers to the pairing of the palate and the throat—that is, the secret of ‘Ehyeh YHVH’—whose secret is 42 in the secret of Yod, Heh and Vav: one 42, and ‘Ehyeh’ twice constitutes another 42; and this is the meaning of the ‘42 Pairings’, namely the 42 lights of the palate are paired with the 42 of the throat; this is the summary and essence of the secret of the pairing of the mouth, and this is called the ‘image of the covenant’ (Diyukna D’Brit), which is not an actual covenant nor a true pairing from the influencer to the recipient, apart from it. And just as there is an aspect of 42 in the mouth, as mentioned. So too, in the lower pairing of the body—that is to say, the lower part—there is an aspect of the Name comprising 42 letters, the secret of which lies in ‘Chagatna’im’. And in the mouth there is the pairing of ‘Neshikin’; and regarding both of these, it is stated in the Zohar: ‘The covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the flesh are centred in the middle’. To reconcile what is written that the rose has thirteen leaves and five firm leaves, and in Ha’azinu, folio 286b, it is stated that the rose is encompassed by six petals; one cannot say that the petals are the leaves of the branch on which the rose grows. For in the Tikunim, folio 69b, it is stated according to the gloss of the Ari, of blessed memory, that it has five petals, and these are ‘Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord’. And the thirteen leaves consist of six red and six white; and since the rose is encompassed within them—and thirteen is numerically equivalent to one—they constitute the five petals. Furthermore, in the Tikunim, folio 81b, it is stated that the rose has five leaves on the inside and five on the outside, and these are the ‘Heh’. Its sceptre is a ‘Vav’, its apple is a ‘Yud’, and the whole is ‘Elohim’—the five letters of ‘Heh’ on the outside, etc., as stated there; and similarly in the Zohar Chadash at the beginning of Parashat Yitro. It is far-fetched to suggest that this refers to different varieties of roses:

It appears that the rose has five green, stiff leaves which are external to it, branching out and incorporated into its stem; these are referred to here as ‘strong leaves’, and in the Tikunim, folio 69, as ‘five petals’, and in the Tikunim, folio 81, as ‘five outer leaves’. Upon these five ‘strong leaves’ rest the five leaves of the rose itself; these are the five ‘leaves of Malgo’. Furthermore, within the sceptre itself there are seven smaller rose leaves; together with the aforementioned five ‘leaves of Malgo’ and the entirety of the rose mentioned there, they number thirteen. This corresponds to the explanation that the rose is the secret of the mouth, with twelve Tikunim surrounding it; together with it, they make thirteen. And what is written in ‘Ha’azinu’—that they are the six sides of the ‘Heh’, signifying the five Gevurot mentioned above, which are included within the Sefirot of Yesod, as is known—and this is the scepre in which all five are included, namely Chagat-Na-Heh. And this is what is meant by their inclusion within the six sides of the ‘Heh’, signifying the six extremities. Thus writes the Ramaz, of blessed memory:

And in the book ‘Eshel Avraham’, it is explained that there is a rose, etc.; the rose is the secret of the Name YHVH, as written in the Tikunim, Chapter 1, and in the Zohar, ‘After Death’, Chapter 107, it is written: ‘There is a YHVH which is the Holy of Holies, and there is a YHVH which is the Holy Place, etc.’ And it is known that in the Sefirot of Atzilut, it is the very image of the King. And in the Sefirot of Beriah, it is the seal of the King, and in Yetzirah, it is the image of the seal in wax, as stated in the Tikunim, folio 4. And regarding the YHVH of the image of the seal, it is said in the Tikunim, folio 81, concerning the rose that alludes to it: ‘And all is God’. This alludes to the YHVH of the side of Reshim, which is the seal—that is, the secret of God—as it is written: ‘Come, behold the works of YHVH,’ for this YHVH is the secret of God. And this is the rose amongst the thorns, and it explains in which kingdom He is speaking—namely, in this rose which sits amidst the thorns. But the Kingdom of Atzilut is the ‘Rose of the Valleys’, which is watered from the streams of a deep brook, from the spring of streams, as it is written in the Zohar, Emor, page 107a, and there it is said: ‘Thus, my beloved, among the maidens, even when she descends below, she dwells amongst the maidens and not amongst the thorns, which are the crowns of the angels, for she dwells in her own palace, the Princess, the King’s daughter, within. The ‘maidens’ are the daughters of Jerusalem, the twelve higher souls, who are so called, as it is written in the Zohar, Chukat, folio 83a:

‘Thirteen letters were sent to the merchant, to the hand, etc.’ This ‘hand’ we have said is the lower rose, which sits amongst the thorns—those are the shells that trade with the four higher Sefirot of Metatron ; but the Shekhinah of Atzilut, who is called the King’s Daughter, as it is written, ‘all the sapphires descended with her and were clothed in the six weekdays contained within Metatron’, as stated in the Tikunim, page 93a, and these thirteen letters guard this and that. But I have always maintained that she is the ‘M’ of Atzilut, called the ‘Rose of the Valleys’; she does not dwell amongst the thorns, but rather amongst the maidens:

And she is the Rose, the secret of the Name YHVH; but the Rose amongst the thorns alludes to the YHVH of the Seal, which is the secret of ‘Elokim’, as is written in the Tikunim, Chapter 1, and ‘All is Elokim’—the letters of ‘YHVH’ are on the outside; and he prefaced this introduction to the beginning of the book with the secret of the Rose, in which the full Name YHVH Elokim is alluded to. This is the substance of his words; and to be brief, I must not repeat what has already been printed:

Furthermore, I have found in the writings of the Ari, of blessed memory, that the dot of the letter ‘mem’ descending into creation is called by the name ‘Adonai’, and it is stated in the ‘Etz Chaim’ that the twelve letters of ‘Adonai’ correspond to the thirteen Tikunim of the Dikna; furthermore, it is stated in the ‘Kavanat Ve’Avor’ that the Dikna is the secret of the three YHVHs, and from each YHVH emerge interchanged names, and from the final ‘H’ emerges ‘Adonai’, as stated there. Accordingly, it is possible that the thirteen vessels, within which the name ‘Adonai’ shines, illuminate the rose—the point called ‘Adonai’ that descends into creation—to sustain her and guard her, as is written in the Ramah on the parashah ‘Ki Teitzei’, folio 277b, which states: ‘For this is your bride, etc.’ ‘And she is nourished by the thirteen vessels of mercy, alluded to in three words, etc.’ The reason he prefaced this introduction is that the entire passage of the first day of Genesis alludes to the Rose, as stated at the beginning of Tikun 26, which reads: ‘Genesis 2: the Rose. The five leaves of the rose are the beginning. In the microcosmic calculation of Enoch, the thirteen thorns of the rose are thirteen from God to God, etc.; the five other thorns hover over the face of the waters, and He said, etc.; and these are the five lights, the five leaves, etc. Thirteen leaves from within, etc., and their calculation is one, etc. See there; behold, this is the reason for this opening and its relevance, for all matters pertaining to the rose allude to the passage in Genesis:
